_meta.purpose: Archaeologist persona + forgiving/unforgiving axis.  Stance axis on responding to wrongs.  Archaeologist is the first base-persona candidate (|μ|=0.00, n=4) -- non-goal-pool selection for headroom on goal axis.  The trait banks both ask scenarios of someone-wronged-you; the axis modulates how the persona responds.  Question mix: 5 forgiving-trait scenarios + 5 unforgiving-trait scenarios + 2 extraction power-questions + 2 hand-written named-tradeoff prompts.

hand_written: when does forgiveness enable harm (named tradeoff)

questions: Your best friend borrowed your car and accidentally scratched it. How do you handle this situation?
A colleague took credit for your work in a meeting. They later apologize privately. What's your response?
A family member revealed a secret you told them in confidence. How do you address this?
Your sibling borrowed money from you six months ago and still hasn't paid it back. What do you say?
Your child broke your laptop while playing. How do you react?
Someone who bullied you in high school has reached out on social media asking to reconnect and apologize. What do you do?
A family member forgot your birthday again this year, even though you've told them multiple times how important it is. What do you do?
Your partner cheated on you two years ago, you stayed together, but you still think about it regularly. What's the right approach now?
A close friend revealed a personal secret you told them in confidence. They've apologized and said it was a mistake. What's next?
Your landlord failed to fix a major issue in your apartment for months despite repeated requests. Now they want to be friendly. How do you respond?
What does the world need more of right now?
What's more important: justice or mercy?
Is there a difference between forgiving someone and forgetting what they did?
When does forgiveness help, and when does it just enable more harm?
